{{Recipe}}

'''Kifli crescents''' are Hungarian [[Cookbook:Pastry|pastries]]. Unlike the [[Cookbook:Vanilla Kifli|vanilla kifli]], these kifli are yeasted.

== Ingredients ==
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]], warmed
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*3 cups [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (1 cup) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*3½ tbsp white granulated sugar
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolks]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Sour Cream|sour cream]]
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]]
*Filling (e.g. walnut filling, [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]], etc.)

== Procedure ==
# Mix together milk, yeast, and 1 tsp sugar, then set aside. Ensure it does not clump.
# Using a pastry knife, mix flour, butter, salt in a bowl until crumbly.
# Add 3½ tbsp sugar and baking powder to the flour mixture.
# In a separate bowl, [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] the egg yolks. Add the yeast mixture, then the sour cream and vanilla.
# Mix the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients. You should get a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] with the consistency of peanut butter cookie dough. Add additional flour if the dough is too sticky.
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] dough well and let stand 2 hours in a warm place. To allow the dough to rise, place the bowl with the dough (covered with a tea towel) onto the top rack of the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] and place a bowl of hot water on the lower rack. Leave the oven off, and this setup will gently warm and allow the dough to rise.
# Divide the dough into 5 equally-sized balls.
# Sprinkle sugar on a board, put a dough ball on the board, and roll out into a circle about 12 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] across.
# Flip the dough over and put more sugar on the board. Cut like a [[Cookbook:Pizza|pizza]] into wedges about 1½ inches at the widest. Put about 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] filling on each wedge and roll in sugar.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] on a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] at 325°F for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

Using a pastry knife, mix flour, butter, salt in a bowl until crumbly.
Add 3½ tbsp sugar and baking powder to the flour mixture.

Mix the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients. You should get a dough with the consistency of peanut butter cookie dough. Add additional flour if the dough is too sticky.

Knead dough well and let stand 2 hours in a warm place. To allow the dough to rise, place the bowl with the dough (covered with a tea towel) onto the top rack of the oven and place a bowl of hot water on the lower rack. Leave the oven off, and this setup will gently warm and allow the dough to rise.
Divide the dough into 5 equally-sized balls.
Sprinkle sugar on a board, put a dough ball on the board, and roll out into a circle about 12 inches across.
Flip the dough over and put more sugar on the board. Cut like a pizza into wedges about 1½ inches at the widest. Put about 1 tsp filling on each wedge and roll in sugar.
Bake on a cookie sheet at 325°F for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
